title: Identity-open normalization and domains of the closed exceptional Hom chain
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$; put $R=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow P$ be a closed immersion of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use ordinary constant-$R$ module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $S_T=\nu_T^*$, $U_T=R\nu_{T,*}$, and $\eta:1\to U_TS_T$ for the specified comparison adjunction [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]; $S_T$ is the exact derived pullback [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. Put $F=i_*^{\mathrm{et}}$, $Q=i_*^{\mathrm{pro}}$, and let $F\dashv I$ be the ordinary etale exceptional adjunction [lem-exc-closed-ambient], with bijection $\beta_{L,N}:\operatorname{Hom}(FL,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L,IN)$. Identify the etale compact-support adjoint for $c=(\mathrm{id}_Z,i)$ with $I$ by the counit-compatible adjunction comparison, and put $J=S_ZIU_P$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Equip $J$ with the specified relative Hom bijections of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] for $c$. Let $H\in D^+(P_{\mathrm{et}},R)$ with $IH\in D^+(Z_{\mathrm{et}},R)$.

Then $IU_PS_PH$ is bounded below, $\alpha_H=S_ZI(\eta_H):S_ZIH\xrightarrow{\sim}JS_PH$ is an isomorphism, and $(IH,\alpha_H)$ is a bounded-below etale-origin witness for $JS_PH$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. For every $L\in D^+(Z_{\mathrm{et}},R)$, under the canonical identity-open identifications, the canonical compact-support comparison $QS_ZL\to S_PFL$ of [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] is $\delta_L^{-1}$, where $\delta_L:S_PFL\xrightarrow{\sim}QS_ZL$ is the named counit-mate comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. The specified relative bijection at the identity witness for $S_ZL$ is exactly the following composite, not merely an unspecified bijection between its endpoints:
$$\begin{aligned}
\Phi_{L,H}:\operatorname{Hom}(QS_ZL,S_PH)&\xrightarrow{g\mapsto g\circ\delta_L}\operatorname{Hom}(S_PFL,S_PH)\\
&\xrightarrow{a\mapsto U_P(a)\circ\eta_{FL}}\operatorname{Hom}(FL,U_PS_PH)\\
&\xrightarrow{\beta_{L,U_PS_PH}}\operatorname{Hom}(L,IU_PS_PH)\\
&\xrightarrow{S_Z}\operatorname{Hom}(S_ZL,JS_PH).
\end{aligned}$$

source.place: Displayed four-factor Hom chain, specialized to the identity-open compactification; domain check and canonical-mate normalization extracted from lem-coef-site-closed-counit-transport, former steps 1 and 2 (agent-written extraction).

proof.text: The coefficient construction [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] makes $R$ a finite commutative ring. The closed immersion $i$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](a), hence separated, of finite type, quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [pqf-lem-proper-basic]. Thus $c=(\mathrm{id}_Z,i)$ is a compactification and the named qcqs direct-image mate applies. Since $Z$ is finite type over the field $k$, [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] gives an integer $d\geq0$ with $\dim Z\leq d$ (take $d=0$ when $Z$ is empty). This checks the geometric and coefficient hypotheses of the bounded comparison-class adjunction used in Step 4. Also $P$ is quasi-compact: its structure map has affine target $\operatorname{Spec}k$ and is quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], whose definition includes this condition in finite type. This checks the proper-case Hom-map definition used below.

source.place: Fixed finite coefficient and compactification hypotheses; Stacks morphisms.tex Tags 01W5 (lemma-closed-immersion-proper) and 01W1 (definition-proper); finite-dimensional compactification required in the stated general Hom normalization.

proof.text: By [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], the actual unit $\eta_H:H\to U_PS_PH$ is an isomorphism. Applying the functor $I$ gives an isomorphism $I(\eta_H):IH\to IU_PS_PH$, with inverse $I(\eta_H^{-1})$: their two composites are identities by functoriality. Therefore $IU_PS_PH$ has the same lower cohomological bound as the assumed bounded-below object $IH$. Applying $S_Z$ gives the isomorphism $\alpha_H$, with inverse $S_ZI(\eta_H^{-1})$. The exact derived pullback [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback] preserves bounded-below objects, so $S_ZIH$ and its isomorphic target $JS_PH$ are bounded below; likewise $S_PH$ and $S_ZL$ are bounded below. The pair $(IH,\alpha_H)$ is now precisely the retained etale-origin witness of [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. No boundedness theorem for $I$ on other inputs has been assumed.

source.place: Domain of the fully faithful comparison in the displayed Hom chain; specialize the comparison unit to H, using the explicit hypothesis IH in D+.

proof.text: Let $C_{c,L}:QS_ZL\to S_PFL$ be the comparison of [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] at the identity witness. Its construction is explicitly fixed in [def-sf-compact-support-site-comparison-construction]: the forward comparison is first the proper counit mate, then the direct image of the exact open-extension comparison, with the canonical associators; $C_{c,L}$ is its inverse. Here the open factor is the identity. To check its map, let $e$ be its component after the canonical identifications of identity extension with the identity functor. Compatibility with composition in [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], applied to $\mathrm{id}_Z\circ\mathrm{id}_Z$, gives $e=e\circ e$. Since $e$ is invertible, cancellation gives $e=1$. The descended termwise comparison is therefore also the identity. The forward compact-support comparison consequently reduces to $b_{i,L}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate], whose defining transpose is the comparison pullback followed by the etale direct-image counit. This is exactly the named $\delta_L$, not a newly chosen isomorphism. Its inverse is $C_{c,L}=\delta_L^{-1}$. The same canonical inclusion identifications are used on both sides.

source.place: First comparison of the displayed Hom chain; Stacks proetale.tex Tag 09AF (lemma-jshriek-comparison), identity open factor, and the counit-mate construction of the proper factor.

proof.text:
Unpack the stipulated relative Hom bijection of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] at the identity witness $(L,1)$ and at $c=(\mathrm{id}_Z,i)$. Its form is fixed in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]: the etale adjunction transported by the compact-support comparison, followed by full faithfulness of $\nu^*$ on $D^+$. Since $J=S_ZIU_P$, passing from $S_PFL$ to the etale adjoint goes through the comparison adjunction $S_P\dashv U_P$, and the etale adjunction is $F\dashv I$ by the counit-compatible identification stipulated in the item. So the bijection precomposes with the inverse of the compact-support comparison $C_{c,L}$, applies the comparison adjunction, then $\beta$, then $S_Z$. Step 3 gives $C_{c,L}^{-1}=\delta_L$. For $g:QS_ZL\to S_PH$ these operations therefore give
$$g\longmapsto g\circ\delta_L\longmapsto U_P(g\circ\delta_L)\circ\eta_{FL}\longmapsto\beta_{L,U_PS_PH}\!\left(U_P(g\circ\delta_L)\circ\eta_{FL}\right)\longmapsto S_Z\!\left(\beta_{L,U_PS_PH}\!\left(U_P(g\circ\delta_L)\circ\eta_{FL}\right)\right).$$
Each arrow is bijective: Step 3 gives the inverse to the first; the next two are the comparison adjunction and $F\dashv I$ of [lem-exc-closed-ambient]; the last is full faithfulness of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], since $L$ and $IU_PS_PH$ are bounded below. Also $FL$ is bounded below by the module direct-image construction [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], so every intermediate Hom is in the stated comparison domain. The unit formula for the second arrow is the defining adjunction formula. The identity origin witness inserts no conjugating arrow. The same four operations define the map $h_{L,S_PH}$ of [def-weil-boundary-exceptional-comparison-data] for $Z\to P$ (its hypotheses were checked in Step 1, and its mate $b$ is the mate defining $\delta_L$). Thus this is exactly the specified bijection, with all four factors retained, rather than a different bijection deduced from right-adjoint uniqueness.

Every non-elementary input is an existing node; no new nodes and no Mathlib leaves.
